definition.description: REV | Ops | Failure Alert. Child flow called from the run-after failed/timed-out path of every flow. Writes one rev_errorlog row and alerts the process owner (FR-010, NFR-016). Holds NO personal data - reference only (NFR-012). See notes.md.

metadata.description: Environment variable. The alert recipient, injected per environment at import (C-TECH-047). Never a literal address.
Environment variable. Outlook fallback recipient used when this flow's own Dataverse or Teams step fails - so a failure of the failure handler is still visible (TAD section 4 fallback).

manual.description: Child-flow trigger. Called only by other flows in this solution, never by a person. Every input is a value the caller already holds - no input requires the caller to read a record.

text.title: Flow name
text.description: The display name of the calling flow, for example REV | Intake | WordPress to Dataverse.

text_1.title: Run id
text_1.description: The calling flow's run identifier, so the native Power Automate run history can be reached from the log row.

text_2.title: Error message
text_2.description: The platform error text. MUST NOT contain personal data. Callers pass the error only, never the payload that caused it.

text_3.title: Record reference
text_3.description: A reference such as REV-2026-014 or the source submission id. A REFERENCE ONLY - never a name, email address or narrative.

text_4.title: Severity
text_4.description: Information, Warning, Error or Critical. Mapped to the rev_errorseverity option value below.

text_5.title: Run link
text_5.description: Deep link to the CALLING flow run in Power Automate. The caller builds it from its own identity - environment id and flow id are only knowable there, not here. NOT required: a caller that omits it still logs and alerts, the link is simply absent.

Map_severity_to_option_value.description: Maps the caller's severity word to the rev_errorseverity option value: 1 Information, 2 Warning, 3 Error, 4 Critical. Anything unrecognised becomes 3 (Error) rather than being dropped - an unclassifiable failure is still a failure.

Truncate_error_message.description: Caps the message at 2000 chars. Defence in depth only (NFR-012) - rev_errorlog has no column that can hold personal data. An unbounded write is the one place a long platform error could leak a payload fragment.
Truncate_error_message.inputs: @if(greater(length(coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_2'], '')), 2000), concat(substring(coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_2'], ''), 0, 2000), ' [truncated]'), coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_2'], 'No error message supplied by the calling flow.'))

Write_error_log_row.description: FR-010. Creates the log row. rev_runurl holds the calling run deep link so the row is actionable from the Error Log itself. Nested item is correct for CreateRecord; only UpdateRecord needs item/<column>. See notes.md.

Alert_process_owner_with_a_card.description: FR-010. Adaptive card carrying an Open this run button. PostCardToConversation has no precedent in this solution, so the HTML message below runs if this fails - the alert is the last thing that should be lost to a shape guess. See notes.md.

parameters.body/messageBody: {"type":"AdaptiveCard","$schema":"http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json","version":"1.4","body":[{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Grant automation failure","wrap":true,"weight":"Bolder","size":"Medium","color":"Attention"},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Flow: @{triggerBody()?['text']}","wrap":true},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Severity: @{triggerBody()?['text_4']}","wrap":true,"spacing":"None"},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Record reference: @{triggerBody()?['text_3']}","wrap":true,"spacing":"None"},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Error log row: @{outputs('Write_error_log_row')?['body/rev_name']}","wrap":true,"spacing":"None"},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Run id: @{triggerBody()?['text_1']}","wrap":true,"spacing":"None"},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"@{outputs('Truncate_error_message')}","wrap":true,"spacing":"Medium"},{"type":"TextBlock","text":"Open the Error Log in REV Grant Administration to mark this resolved.","wrap":true,"isSubtle":true,"size":"Small","spacing":"Medium"}],"actions":[{"type":"Action.OpenUrl","title":"Open this run in Power Automate","url":"@{triggerBody()?['text_5']}"}]}

Alert_process_owner_in_Teams.description: Fallback for the card above. Same content as plain HTML with a link instead of a button, so a rejected card payload still reaches the process owner. See notes.md.

parameters.body/messageBody:
Grant automation failure

Flow: @{triggerBody()?['text']}
Severity: @{triggerBody()?['text_4']}
Record reference: @{triggerBody()?['text_3']}
Error log row: @{outputs('Write_error_log_row')?['body/rev_name']}
Run id: @{triggerBody()?['text_1']}

@{outputs('Truncate_error_message')}

@{if(empty(coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_5'], '')), '

No run link was supplied by the calling flow. Find the run by its id in the Power Automate run history.

', concat('

Open this run in Power Automate

'))}

Open the Error Log in REV Grant Administration to mark this resolved.

Fallback_email_when_logging_or_alerting_.description: A failure of the failure handler must not be silent. If the Dataverse write or Teams post fails, email the service mailbox instead (TAD section 4). No record reference: not guaranteed safely bounded here; the run id lets the recipient find the run.

parameters.emailMessage/Subject: Grant automation: failure alert could not be logged
parameters.emailMessage/Body:
REV | Ops | Failure Alert could not write to the Error Log table or could not post to Teams.

Calling flow: @{triggerBody()?['text']}
Calling run id: @{triggerBody()?['text_1']}
Severity reported: @{triggerBody()?['text_4']}

Investigate in the Power Automate run history. The original failure is NOT recorded in Dataverse.

Respond_to_calling_flow.description: Always responds 200, even on failure: the parent has ALREADY failed, and the error handler must not turn one failure into two. A child flow needs a Response or the parent hangs until timeout. Body says whether the row was written, for run-history review.
